partners.mechanism_chain: PKLR (HGNC:9040) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis (KEGG:00010); Glycolysis (KEGG:00010) —INCREASES→ ATP (CHEBI:15422); ATP (CHEBI:15422) —DECREASES→ Cellular energy homeostasis (GO:0006695); Cellular energy homeostasis (GO:0006695) —LEADS_TO→ Pyruvate kinase deficiency anemia (HP:0001880); ACACA (HGNC:2) —DISRUPTS→ Fatty acid biosynthesis (KEGG:00061); Fatty acid biosynthesis (KEGG:00061) —DECREASES→ Acetyl-CoA (CHEBI:15359); Acetyl-CoA (CHEBI:15359) —DECREASES→ Cellular energy homeostasis (GO:0006695); Cellular energy homeostasis (GO:0006695) —LEADS_TO→ Metabolic encephalopathy (HP:0012131). Gain-of-function mutations in PKLR lead to hyperactivity of pyruvate kinase, resulting in increased flux through glycolysis and thus elevated ATP production. However, this hyperactivity can disrupt normal metabolic flux and lead to anemia. Conversely, loss-of-function mutations in ACACA impair the conversion of Acetyl-CoA to Malonyl-CoA, a critical step in fatty acid synthesis. This leads to a reduction in available Acetyl-CoA for other pathways and a deficit in ATP production, contributing to metabolic encephalopathy. Both increased and decreased ATP production, stemming from distinct genetic origins, ultimately converge on disrupting cellular energy homeostasis.

partners.diseaseBName: neurodevelopmental disorder with visual defects and brain anomalies
partners.mechanism_chain: Pyruvate Kinase (PKLR) (HGNC:9027) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis (GO:0006096); Glycolysis (GO:0006096) —LEADS_TO→ Pyruvate kinase hyperactivity (MONDO:0007067); Hexokinase 1 (HK1) (HGNC:4965) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis (GO:0006096); Glycolysis (GO:0006096) —PRODUCES→ ATP (CHEBI:15422); ATP (CHEBI:15422) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodevelopmental disorder with visual defects and brain anomalies (MONDO:0032807). Gain-of-function mutations in PKLR (Pyruvate Kinase) lead to hyperactivity of the enzyme, increasing flux through glycolysis and thus ATP production, manifesting as pyruvate kinase hyperactivity (Disease A). Loss-of-function mutations in HK1 (Hexokinase 1), a rate-limiting enzyme in glycolysis, impair glucose phosphorylation and subsequent ATP production, contributing to neurodevelopmental defects (Disease B). Both disease mechanisms converge on the central role of glycolysis and ATP production, albeit with opposing functional consequences on these pathways.

falsification.text: If genetic studies reveal that the causal variants for pyruvate kinase hyperactivity (Disease A) are exclusively loss-of-function and do not affect glycolytic flux or ATP production, or if the causal variants for neurodevelopmental disorder with visual defects and brain anomalies (Disease B) are exclusively gain-of-function mutations in HK1 that paradoxically increase ATP production, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, if specific biomarkers of glycolytic flux or ATP levels are found to be diametrically opposed in affected individuals of both diseases in a manner inconsistent with the proposed functional directions, it would also serve as a falsification.
falsification.gnomad_variant: rs767342313 (a known pathogenic variant in PKLR) is found at a frequency >0.001 in gnomAD.
